doc.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Chico Hamilton quintet reunion album and Jim Hall's absence
summary: Audio of the 'Reunion' album; he explains the reunion arose from a Verona promoter's request, and Jim Hall declined.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So are you a flutist too?
I wanted to play a little piece, as long as we’re on the subject.
This is, yeah. I wish I could write that way too.
Good point. It’s great. That was like, I just love that. Like how did he know to do that right then? It just seems to fit so well.
Well we knew each other pretty well. See he’ll change tempos anytime, and as you know with the way time is, I could play slow or fast, and he could [scats].
Right, so this is off the “Reunion” album. And you had just about, let’s see, for the exception of one fellow, this was the original —
Except for Jim Hall. He had John Pisano. The other guys were all there. But Jim wouldn’t go, he didn’t want to go back.
He didn’t want to go back to re-visit something.

Yeah. He liked Chico and they liked each other but he didn’t want to go with any of that anymore. Well I understand in a way, it was a big switch. I went back only because I set this up when I was in Europe. Nicolo from Verona, a guy that does jazz there, he said, “Who can you bring here that would get a big crowd?” And I was just being as truthful as I could by saying, “Well I could bring my group but in order to get a big crowd you’d do better with the Chico Hamilton quintet because the band never got to Europe when we

were playing before. So he got excited right then. He said, “You think you can get him?” I said if I can talk to Chico to do it, because Chico’s not playing that way now. He only plays that way if we meet up. But he likes doing that. In fact he wanted just to do that, he and I would go to Europe, and play like that every night. I said no because I’d lose too much, meaning that after a while you want some other horns to come in. But we can do that in between.
Yeah that’s the beauty of that, it’s a change in texture.

And sometimes it’s unbelievable. This was good. We did a thing at my birthday party about four or five years ago at the Wadsworth Theater, and we had the band there and a lot of bands, and all of a sudden when he got on he looked at me and I knew he wanted to do one of those. And we did one that was unbelievable also.
